questions.question: Bushu, Yemshe and Tokhu Emong are some of the cultural festivals celebrated by the tribal people of which state?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Nagaland**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Bushu, Yemshe, and Tokhu Emong** are major cultural festivals celebrated by the tribal communities of Nagaland.
 
• **Tokhu Emong** is celebrated by the Lotha Naga tribe as a post-harvest festival to mark the end of the agricultural season.
 
• **Bushu** is a festival of the Kachari tribe, celebrated to mark the end of the paddy cultivation cycle.
 
• **Yemshe** is observed by the Pochury tribe as a harvest festival, signifying a time of joy and thanksgiving.
 
• Nagaland is known as the **‘Land of Festivals’** due to its diverse tribal communities, each having unique cultural practices and traditions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nagaland's Tribal Diversity**

 
 
• Nagaland is home to 16 major tribes, including Ao, Angami, Sumi, Lotha, Chakhesang, and Konyak tribes, among others.
 
• Each tribe has its unique dialect, attire, customs, and festivals, contributing to the state's rich cultural heritage.
 
 
 
• **Hornbill Festival**
 
 
• This is the most famous cultural festival of Nagaland, celebrated annually in December.
 
• It showcases the cultural vibrancy of all tribes and is often referred to as the **‘Festival of Festivals’**.
 
• The festival includes traditional dance, music, handicrafts, and cuisine, attracting tourists from around the world.
 
 
 
• **Geography of Nagaland**
 
 
• Nagaland is located in Northeast India and shares its borders with Assam, Arunachal Pradesh, Manipur, and Myanmar.
 
• Kohima is the state capital, while Dimapur is the largest city and a major commercial hub.
 
 
 
• **Traditional Practices**
 
 
• Many festivals in Nagaland are closely linked to agricultural cycles, emphasizing the importance of farming in their livelihood.
 
• Traditional attire, dances, and songs during festivals reflect the deep-rooted cultural identity of the tribes.

questions.question: Ostriches were found in India during which period?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Palaeolithic**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Ostrich fossils and eggshell fragments have been discovered in several archaeological sites across India, particularly in the **Palaeolithic period**.
 
• Evidence of ostriches in India has been primarily found in regions such as Rajasthan, Gujarat, and Madhya Pradesh.
 
• These fossils suggest that ostriches were once a part of the Indian subcontinent's fauna during the late Pleistocene epoch.
 
• The Palaeolithic period, which spans from approximately 2.5 million years ago to 10,000 years ago, is marked by the use of stone tools and the emergence of early human behavior.
 
• Ostrich remains in India have been studied using radiocarbon dating and other scientific methods to establish their Palaeolithic context.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Palaeolithic Period:**

 
 
• The Palaeolithic period is also known as the Old Stone Age.
 
• It is characterized by the use of crude stone tools and the subsistence lifestyle of hunter-gatherers.
 
• This period is divided into three phases: Lower, Middle, and Upper Palaeolithic.
 
 
 
• **Ostrich Evidence in India:**
 
 
• Ostrich eggshells and fossilized bones have been unearthed in sites such as Bhimbetka and Patne in India.
 
• These findings indicate the presence of ostriches in the Indian subcontinent during the Pleistocene epoch.
 
 
 
• **Scientific Techniques Used:**
 
 
• Techniques such as radiocarbon dating and isotopic analysis are used to analyze ostrich remains.
 
• These methods help determine the age and environmental conditions of the period.
 
 
 
• **Pleistocene Epoch:**
 
 
• The Pleistocene epoch (2.58 million to 11,700 years ago) is a geological timeframe that witnessed significant climatic changes and the evolution of early humans.
 
• It coincides with the Palaeolithic period in archaeological terms.

questions.question: According to the Indian Constitution, which of the following powers are NOT vested in Governor?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Writs Issuing powers**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Governor of a state in India does not have the power to issue writs. **Writ-issuing powers are exclusively vested in the Supreme Court and High Courts under Articles 32 and 226 of the Indian Constitution, respectively.**
 
• The writs include Habeas Corpus, Mandamus, Prohibition, Certiorari, and Quo Warranto, designed to ensure the protection of fundamental rights and maintain justice.
 
• Governors exercise various powers, including **Legislative, Financial, Executive, and Discretionary powers**, but lack judicial powers like issuing writs.
 
• Writ jurisdiction is a crucial judicial function and cannot be delegated to executive authorities like the Governor.
 
• This separation of powers ensures checks and balances in governance, safeguarding the independence of the judiciary.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 32:**

 
 
• Known as the "Right to Constitutional Remedies," it empowers the Supreme Court to issue writs to enforce fundamental rights.
 
• It is considered the heart and soul of the Indian Constitution, as stated by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar.
 
 
 
• **Article 226:**
 
 
• Empowers High Courts to issue writs for the enforcement of fundamental rights as well as other legal rights.
 
• The scope of writ jurisdiction under Article 226 is broader than under Article 32.
 
 
 
• **Governor's Powers:**
 
 
• **Legislative Powers:** Includes summoning, proroguing, and dissolving the state legislature and reserving bills for the President.
 
• **Financial Powers:** Includes ensuring the presentation of the state budget and recommending money bills.
 
• **Discretionary Powers:** Includes decision-making in cases such as hung assemblies or reserved bills.
 
 
 
• **Judiciary's Independence:**
 
 
• The judiciary in India is an independent body, separate from the executive and legislative branches.
 
• This ensures the fair and impartial administration of justice and the protection of constitutional rights.

questions.question: Which type of industry uses natural resources with minimal human intervention and is oriented towards nature?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Primary Industry**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Primary industries** focus on the extraction and harvesting of natural resources directly from nature, such as agriculture, forestry, fishing, and mining.
 
• These industries operate with minimal human intervention and rely heavily on natural processes.
 
• Examples include farming, logging, fishing, and mineral extraction, which form the base for secondary and tertiary industries.
 
• Primary industries are integral to the economy as they provide raw materials for manufacturing and other industrial sectors.
 
• They are characterized by their direct interaction with nature, making them highly dependent on environmental conditions and sustainability practices.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Types of Industries:**

 
 
• **Primary Industry:** Focuses on the extraction of natural resources (e.g., agriculture, fishing, forestry).
 
• **Secondary Industry:** Involves manufacturing and processing of raw materials into finished goods.
 
• **Tertiary Industry:** Provides services such as retail, transportation, and healthcare.
 
• **Quaternary Industry:** Focuses on knowledge-based services, including information technology, research, and consultancy.
 
 
 
• **Natural Resources:**
 
 
• Materials provided by nature that are used in economic activities, such as water, minerals, forests, and soil.
 
• Renewable resources (e.g., solar energy, wind energy) can replenish naturally, while non-renewable resources (e.g., fossil fuels, metals) are finite.
 
 
 
• **Environmental Dependency:**
 
 
• Primary industries depend heavily on environmental factors like climate, soil fertility, and water availability.
 
• Sustainable practices are crucial to ensure long-term viability and prevent resource depletion.
 
 
 
• **Role in Economy:**
 
 
• Primary industries are foundational to the economy, providing essential inputs for secondary and tertiary sectors.
 
• They contribute significantly to employment, especially in rural areas, and are critical for food security and resource supply.

questions.question: Which Five-Year Plan was interrupted due to the Indo-Pak War and economic crisis?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Third Plan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Third Five-Year Plan (1961-1966) aimed to achieve self-reliance in food production and industrial growth in India.
 
• This plan was interrupted due to the **Indo-China War of 1962** and the **Indo-Pak War of 1965**, causing economic turmoil.
 
• The government shifted focus from planned economic development to **defense and emergency management**.
 
• Severe droughts in 1965-1966 also further disrupted the objectives of the plan, leading to a crisis in agricultural production.
 
• The economic challenges during this period necessitated a deviation from the planned targets and resulted in the introduction of annual plans or "Plan Holidays" from 1966 to 1969.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Five-Year Plans in India**

 
 
• India's Five-Year Plans were a series of centralized economic and social development strategies implemented from 1951 to 2017.
 
• The Planning Commission was responsible for formulating these plans until its replacement by the NITI Aayog in 2015.
 
• The plans aimed to boost economic growth, improve the standard of living, and address social inequalities.
 
 
 
• **Plan Holidays (1966-1969)**
 
 
• Plan Holidays were introduced after the Third Five-Year Plan due to financial constraints caused by wars and droughts.
 
• During this period, the government adopted annual plans to address short-term goals and stabilize the economy.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Indo-Pak War on Economy**
 
 
• The 1965 Indo-Pak War strained India's financial resources, diverting funds from developmental activities to defense expenditures.
 
• It disrupted trade and led to inflation, further complicating economic recovery efforts.
 
 
 
• **Green Revolution**
 
 
• The Green Revolution, initiated in the late 1960s, was a response to the agricultural crisis during the Third Plan era.
 
• It focused on high-yield crop varieties, modern irrigation techniques, and the use of fertilizers to increase agricultural productivity.

questions.question: In September, the Union Cabinet approved the One Nation, One Poll recommendations proposed by whom among the following?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Union Cabinet approved the **One Nation, One Poll** recommendations proposed by a committee led by former President **Ram Nath Kovind** in September 2023.
 
• This initiative seeks to synchronize the timing of Lok Sabha and State Assembly elections to reduce the frequency of elections and associated costs.
 
• The government formed the committee under Ram Nath Kovind's chairmanship to examine the feasibility of implementing the "One Nation, One Poll" policy.
 
• The proposal aims to enhance administrative efficiency, reduce the burden on security forces, and ensure seamless governance by avoiding frequent imposition of the Model Code of Conduct.
 
• The committee includes legal experts, political leaders, and representatives from various government bodies to ensure the recommendations are comprehensive and inclusive.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **One Nation, One Poll:**

 
 
• This concept refers to holding simultaneous elections for the Lok Sabha, State Legislative Assemblies, and local bodies across the country.
 
• It aims to reduce election-related expenses and frequent disruptions to development activities caused by repeated imposition of the Model Code of Conduct.
 
• The idea was first proposed during the tenure of Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee and has been discussed multiple times in recent years.
 
 
 
• **Committee Formation:**
 
 
• In 2023, the Union Government set up a high-level committee under the chairmanship of Ram Nath Kovind to deliberate on the feasibility of implementing this electoral reform.
 
• The committee includes members from political parties, legal experts, and representatives from the Election Commission of India (ECI).
 
 
 
• **Advantages of One Nation, One Poll:**
 
 
• Reduction in the cost of conducting frequent elections.
 
• Minimization of policy paralysis and disruptions in governance caused by repeated elections.
 
• Streamlining of security personnel deployment and efficient management of resources.
 
 
 
• **Challenges:**
 
 
• Constitutional amendments are required to synchronize the terms of various legislative bodies.
 
• Political consensus is necessary to implement the reform successfully.
 
• Logistical challenges such as voter education, preparedness of the Election Commission, and managing simultaneous elections on a large scale.

questions.question: Which climate zone is characterised by hot and humid conditions throughout the year?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tropical**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Tropical climate zones are characterized by **hot and humid conditions throughout the year**.
 
• They are located near the **Equator**, between the Tropic of Cancer and Tropic of Capricorn.
 
• These regions receive a high amount of solar radiation, resulting in consistently warm temperatures and **minimal seasonal variation.**
 
• Tropical zones experience **significant rainfall** due to their proximity to Intertropical Convergence Zones (ITCZ), which facilitates frequent precipitation.
 
• Examples of tropical climates include the **Amazon rainforest**, the Congo Basin, and Southeast Asia.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Intertropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ)**

 
 
• A region near the Equator where **trade winds converge**, leading to frequent thunderstorms and heavy rainfall.
 
• The ITCZ shifts seasonally, influencing precipitation patterns in tropical regions.
 
 
 
• **Rainforest Ecosystem**
 
 
• Tropical rainforests are characterized by **high biodiversity**, with millions of species of plants, animals, and microorganisms.
 
• They serve as the **Earth's lungs** by producing oxygen and absorbing carbon dioxide.
 
 
 
• **Temperature Range**
 
 
• In tropical climates, the average monthly temperature typically stays above **18°C (64°F)** year-round.
 
• This contrasts with other climate zones where seasonal temperature variations are more pronounced.
 
 
 
• **Subtypes of Tropical Climate**
 
 
• **Tropical rainforest climate:** High rainfall throughout the year.
 
• **Tropical monsoon climate:** Seasonal shifts between wet and dry periods.
 
• **Tropical savanna climate:** Wet summers and dry winters.

questions.question: A geographic region that has separate but similar ecosystems characterised by a distinct climate is called a(n) ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**biome**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A biome is a large geographic area characterized by specific **climatic conditions**, flora, and fauna.
 
• Biomes are classified based on their distinct ecosystems, such as forests, deserts, grasslands, tundra, and aquatic environments.
 
• Factors like temperature, precipitation, altitude, and latitude play a significant role in determining the type of biome.
 
• Examples of biomes include the Amazon rainforest (tropical rainforest biome) and the Sahara Desert (desert biome).
 
• Unlike ecosystems, which focus on interactions within a smaller area, biomes represent broader climatic and ecological patterns.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ecosystem**

 
 
• An ecosystem is a community of living organisms in conjunction with non-living components like air, water, and soil.
 
• It focuses on the interactions and energy flow between biotic (living) and abiotic (non-living) components within a specific area.
 
• Examples include ponds, forests, coral reefs, and grasslands.
 
 
 
• **Biosphere**
 
 
• The biosphere is the global sum of all ecosystems and includes all life forms on Earth.
 
• It extends to the atmosphere, lithosphere, and hydrosphere where living organisms exist.
 
• The biosphere supports life by cycling nutrients, water, and energy.
 
 
 
• **Climate**
 
 
• Climate refers to the long-term average weather conditions in a particular region.
 
• It is determined by factors like temperature, humidity, wind patterns, and precipitation over decades.
 
• Climate greatly influences the type of biome that forms in a specific area.
 
 
 
• **Organism**
 
 
• An organism is any individual living entity, such as a plant, animal, fungus, or microbe.
 
• Organisms are the basic unit of life in biology, interacting within ecosystems and biomes.
 
• They adapt to their environment to survive and reproduce.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Debendranath Tagore** founded the Tattwabodhini Sabha in Bengal in **1839**.
 
• The Sabha aimed to **revive the principles of the Brahmo Samaj**, emphasizing monotheism and the Upanishadic philosophy.
 
• The Tattwabodhini Sabha became a hub for discussions on **social and religious reforms** in Bengal.
 
• It also played a significant role in promoting **Bengali language and literature** by publishing the "Tattwabodhini Patrika," a journal that propagated reformist ideas.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Brahmo Samaj:**

 
 
• Founded by Raja Ram Mohan Roy in 1828, it was a socio-religious reform movement that opposed idol worship and emphasized monotheism.
 
• The Brahmo Samaj sought to reform Hinduism by eliminating practices like sati, caste discrimination, and child marriage.

questions.question: Thanjavur Quartet is best remembered for the revival and codification of which ancient classical dance form?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bharatanatyam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Thanjavur Quartet refers to four brothers—Chinnayya, Ponnayya, Sivanandam, and Vadivelu—renowned for their contribution to Bharatanatyam.
 
• They were instrumental in reviving, codifying, and systematizing Bharatanatyam as a classical art form during the early 19th century.
 
• They composed numerous dance pieces, including varnams and padams, that became integral to the Bharatanatyam repertoire.
 
• The brothers served in the court of King Serfoji II of Thanjavur and were deeply influenced by his patronage of the arts.
 
• Their efforts laid the foundation for the margam (traditional sequence of Bharatanatyam performance), which is still followed today.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bharatanatyam:**

 
 
• Bharatanatyam is one of the oldest classical dance forms of India, originating in Tamil Nadu.
 
• It combines bhava (expression), raga (melody), tala (rhythm), and natyam (dramatic art).
 
• Traditionally performed in temples as an offering to deities, it is deeply rooted in spiritual and religious themes.
 
• The dance is accompanied by Carnatic music, and its movements are characterized by intricate footwork and graceful gestures.
 
 
 
• **Thanjavur Quartet's Legacy:**
 
 
• The Quartet's compositions are still widely performed and respected in Bharatanatyam recitals.
 
• They introduced innovations such as integrating music with dance and enhancing the use of abhinaya (expressive storytelling).
 
 
 
• **Margam:**
 
 
• Margam is the traditional sequence of a Bharatanatyam performance, consisting of pieces like alarippu, jatiswaram, varnam, padam, and tillana.
 
• This structure was formalized by the Thanjavur Quartet, making it a hallmark of Bharatanatyam.
 
 
 
• **King Serfoji II:**
 
 
• King Serfoji II of Thanjavur was a major patron of the arts, encouraging the development of Bharatanatyam under the Thanjavur Quartet.
 
• His reign saw a flourishing of Tamil classical music, dance, and literature.

questions.question: A balanced budget refers to a situation where:

__
 
• A balanced budget occurs when **government revenue is equal to its expenditure**, ensuring no deficit or surplus in the budget.
 
• This fiscal arrangement reflects **efficient financial management** by the government, maintaining economic stability.
 
• Balanced budgets are often preferred as they avoid excessive borrowing and ensure **sustainability of public finances.**
 
• Such budgets are typically used as a tool to **prevent inflation or deflation** in the economy.
 
• While balanced budgets are ideal, they may not always be feasible, especially during times of economic recession or financial crises.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Budget Deficit:**

 
 
• A situation where government expenditure exceeds its revenue.
 
• It often requires borrowing or issuing bonds to cover the gap.
 
 
 
• **Budget Surplus:**
 
 
• Occurs when government revenue exceeds expenditure.
 
• Surpluses can be used for debt repayment or saved for future use.
 
 
 
• **Fiscal Policy:**
 
 
• A government strategy for managing its budget through revenue collection (taxes) and expenditure.
 
• Fiscal policy plays a crucial role in regulating economic growth and stability.
 
 
 
• **Types of Government Budgets:**
 
 
• Balanced Budget: Revenue equals expenditure.
 
• Surplus Budget: Revenue exceeds expenditure.
 
• Deficit Budget: Expenditure exceeds revenue.
 
 
 
• **Implications of a Balanced Budget:**
 
 
• Promotes fiscal discipline and long-term economic stability.
 
• May limit the government’s ability to invest in large-scale projects during critical times.

questions.question: According to the Constitution, India is a _____________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Union of States**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• According to Article 1 of the Indian Constitution, India is defined as a **"Union of States."**
 
• The term "Union of States" signifies that India is not a federation created by an agreement among states but rather an indestructible union.
 
• The Indian Constitution does not describe India as a federation, although it has federal features. It is instead called a "quasi-federal" system.
 
• The central government holds more power compared to the states, ensuring a strong unitary character.
 
• This structure aims to maintain the unity and integrity of India while allowing states to function within their designated powers under the Constitution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Federal Features of the Indian Constitution:**

 
 
• Division of powers between the Union and States through the Union List, State List, and Concurrent List.
 
• Independent judiciary with the Supreme Court as the guardian of the Constitution.
 
• Written Constitution with rigid provisions requiring special procedures for amendments.
 
• Bicameral legislature at the central level (Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha).
 
 
 
• **Unitary Features:**
 
 
• Strong central authority with residuary powers vested in the Union Government.
 
• Emergency provisions that convert India into a unitary state during crises.
 
• Single citizenship for all Indians, emphasizing unity.
 
• Integrated judiciary and administrative system across the country.
 
 
 
• **Terminology:**
 
 
• "Union of States" reflects the emphasis on the unity of the nation despite regional diversities.
 
• "Quasi-federal" refers to the blend of federal and unitary characteristics in the Indian political system.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context:**
 
 
• The framers of the Constitution chose the term "Union" to prevent the possibility of secession by states, unlike in some federations.
 
• This was influenced by the partition of India and the need to ensure national integration.

questions.question: How many indicators were included in National Multidimensional Poverty Index 2021 of India?

__
 
• The National Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) 2021 of India is based on **12 indicators**.
 
• These indicators are grouped under three dimensions: **Health, Education, and Standard of Living**.
 
• The MPI report is prepared by **NITI Aayog** in collaboration with Oxford Poverty and Human Development Initiative (OPHI) and United Nations Development Programme (UNDP).
 
• Indicators include nutrition, child mortality, years of schooling, school attendance, cooking fuel, sanitation, drinking water, electricity, housing, assets, and others.
 
• The MPI aims to provide a comprehensive measure of poverty beyond income-based metrics.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI)**

 
 
• It is a measure developed by OPHI and UNDP to capture multidimensional aspects of poverty.
 
• MPI complements income-based poverty measures by assessing deprivations across multiple dimensions like health, education, and living standards.
 
• It uses household-level data to analyze poverty trends and identify areas requiring policy intervention.
 
 
 
• **NITI Aayog**
 
 
• It is the policy think tank of the Government of India, established in 2015 to replace the Planning Commission.
 
• NITI Aayog is responsible for promoting cooperative federalism and providing strategic and technical advice to states and central governments.
 
 
 
• **Key Dimensions of MPI in India**
 
 
• **Health:** Includes indicators like nutrition and child mortality.
 
• **Education:** Covers years of schooling and school attendance.
 
• **Living Standards:** Includes indicators like access to electricity, sanitation, drinking water, housing, cooking fuel, and assets.
 
 
 
• **Global MPI**
 
 
• The Global Multidimensional Poverty Index is published annually by OPHI and UNDP.
 
• It covers more than 100 countries and provides global insights into poverty trends.

questions.question: The LCM of 2³ × 9² × 13, 2² × 13² × 19 and 9³ × 13² × 19² is :-

To find the LCM of numbers given in exponential form, identify all the distinct bases.

Then, take the highest power of each distinct base present across all the given expressions.

The highest powers present for each base are: 2³, 9³, 13², and 19².

Multiply these highest powers together to get the final LCM directly.

**∴ The correct answer is 2³ × 9³ × 13² × 19².**

For any two numbers a and b, the product of their HCF and LCM is strictly equal to the product of the numbers themselves: HCF(a, b) × LCM(a, b) = a × b.

Constant multiple = q₁ ÷ p₁ = 630 ÷ 15 = 42
